newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end steady but Roche jumps on sales.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end steady but Roche jumps on sales.

text.p: Swiss shares ended little changed on Tuesday in quiet trade, dealers said.

Roche, one of the few winners, profited from better than expected second quarter sales figures announced pre-bourse. Roche sales doubled speed for a first-half gain of 20 percent. The stock advanced 140 francs to 14,425.
Profit-taking and pressure from derivative-related selling initially pushed overall prices lower, dealers said. Later, derivative-related pressure steamed off.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) down 0.02 percent or 1.1 points at 5,844.7 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 0.05 percent or 1.71 points at 3,685.40.
Volume leader Novartis, whose shares were lower in early trade, advanced eight francs to end at 2,417.

Shares of insurer Zuerich rose four francs to 603. One dealer said the shares found support around 600 francs, bouyed as well by some switching from recent bourse star Winterthur. Winterthur dropped five francs to 1,469 after recent steep gains, still 90 percent above levels at the start of the year.
Technology group Sulzer was under pressure. The stock lost 36 francs to 1,200.

Shares of Sulzer Medica, which were traded on Monday for the first time, closed eight francs higher at 416. One dealer said there might have been some switches to Sulzer Medica fropm parent Sulzer. The issue price of Sulzer Medica was 350 francs.
Market sentiment was good and traders said the outlook would remain positive if the interest rate environment stayed stable.
The market paid little attention to SBC's announcement of a strategic alliance with Japanese bank LTCB, one dealer said. SBC lost 4.50 francs to 410.
